title: Vesuvius buries Pompeii and Herculaneum
summary: The eruption of Vesuvius in 79 CE buried Pompeii, Herculaneum and nearby settlements. Buildings and artifacts preserved beneath volcanic material now provide evidence of life in Roman towns.

The disaster created an unusually rich but selective archaeological record. It illuminates domestic and commercial settings while reminding us that survival of evidence can depend on catastrophic circumstances.
